data.title: Autophagy Flux Is Remodeled Sex- and Cell Type-Specifically During Human Aging, and Is Linked to Reduced Physical Function in Older Adults
data.authors: Moreno TM; Kumsta C et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human primary dermal fibroblasts, induced neurons (iNs), PBMCs (healthy aging cohort, pilot exercise intervention)
data.finding: Autophagy flux in humans is remodeled with age in a sex- and cell-type-specific way, uncoupled from autophagy-gene transcription; in adults over 70, higher PBMC autophagy flux associates with reduced physical function, and 12 weeks of mild exercise lowers PBMC flux while improving function.
data.abstract_excerpt: Autophagy is widely proposed to decline with age; however, direct evidence across human cell types remains limited. Moreover, it is unclear whether age-associated changes in autophagy-gene transcription are accompanied by corresponding changes in autophagic activity, and whether autophagic activity relates to physiological function during aging. We performed transcriptomic and functional autophagy analyses across subject-matched human cell types from a healthy aging cohort.
